# Independent root audit: weighted centroidal planar chords

The proof in candidate c22519c29667168e passes the root
review. This audit concerns the auxiliary planar theorem only.

- The finite weight LP reduces to a noncollinear positive triple or one
  opposite pair. Boundary uniqueness on each ray makes opposite-ray pairs
  exactly antipodal, with equal weights.
- Positive dependence and theta_i<1/2 make all six marked points vertices
  of their central hexagon. The explicit coordinates p1=(1,0), p2=(0,1),
  p3=(-a,-b) give exactly the three strict triangle inequalities stated.
- Each heavy cut retains all marked points. For a nonsupporting line its
  two marked boundary points are the endpoints of its line section; radial
  projection proves that every deleted point has the correct angular cost.
  The three explicit heavy-edge normals and their positive dependence have
  been checked algebraically. Their reflected halfplanes give the other
  hexagon edges, so T intersect (-T)=H and K' lies between H and T.
- In barycentric coordinates the reflected constraints are lambda_i<=2l_i.
  Thus the three missing corners have relative areas t_i^2 and H has area
  2e. The cyclic endpoint formulas sum to 2 sum l_i v_i=0 for each opposite
  pair. The coefficient of v_i in the claimed weighted dependence is
  (1-t_i)/2=l_i. The orientation determinant selects precisely corner i.
- The corner-area box enlargement is safe: no assertion of realizability
  is needed. The denominator is positive throughout this box.
- All eight polynomial cases were independently derived by the root before
  receiving the final note. In particular the singleton square completion
  and its v-endpoint case, and the two-corner linear-v formula, are exact.
  The full-corner identity E=e-9t0t1t2 is also checked.
- Gauge regularization keeps BOTH signs of every marked chord on the new
  boundary, rescales the balancing weights consistently, and leaves cap
  orientations fixed. Hausdorff/L1 convergence passes the exact inequality.
- Closed cap boundaries are area-null here, and triangle equality satisfies
  every section-centroid and balance hypothesis.

The conclusion is a genuine weighted stationary-section inequality in
continuous dimension two. It is not an OC proof: independent fiber affine
variations and compatibility forces remain separate issues in its mixed
applications, and no higher-dimensional analogue is assumed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
